title: Patch: a Fuse that is attacked strikes back with its plain attack, since only its own attacks are multiplied
thread:
**Issue #4156 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4156: Patch: a Fuse that is attacked strikes back with its plain attack, since only its own attacks are multiplied
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Fuse is a small Unit whose own attacks hit five times as hard in its lane and three times as hard in the lanes beside it. Today the game also applies that multiplier when Fuse is the one being attacked. An enemy 6/6 that attacks a Fuse across the lane takes 10 damage back and dies. The card's text and the rules give it 2, and Fuse would take 3 after its Armor. A Radiant Fuse hits back for 28. The preview players see before attacking, the lethal hint and the practice AI all show the same wrong number, so players and the AI both learn to leave Fuse alone. After the fix, a Fuse that is attacked hits back for its printed attack, and its own attacks sweep exactly as they do now.

## Why

- The rule: §4.3 (`spec/04-combat.md:46`) and §6.3's Sweep row (`spec/06-keywords.md:185`) say "its attack hits every enemy Unit in its lane for 5 times its attack (Radiant 7) and every enemy Unit in the adjacent lanes for 3 times (Radiant 4)". R3554008 says the same, and the card's text (`stinkyscapeplus-107` in `crates/cards/catalog.json`) reads "Its attacks deal {sweepLane}x damage to enemy Units in this lane, {sweepAdjacent}x in adjacent lanes." Nothing gives Fuse's strike back a weight. Lane strike (M #97.5 Bunker, `spec/04-combat.md:44`) is different on purpose: it applies "in combat with the opposing Unit", attacking or defending, and Bunker's tests hold its strike back at 3 times.
- The bug: `crates/engine/src/combat.rs:921` multiplies the defender's strike back by `lane_multiplier_for(defender, attacker)`. Since R3554008, that function returns `sweep_weight` first (`combat.rs:703`). `sweep_weight` (`combat.rs:667`) checks only that the two Units are on opposite sides with lanes that meet or sit one apart. It never asks which one attacked. So a defending Fuse gets half a sweep: its attacker alone takes the weight, and the rest of its lane takes nothing, because `sweep()` runs only on Fuse's own attack. Neither reading of the rules gives that result.
- How much it changes: Fuse is Ranged, so it strikes back at every attacker, Ranged ones included (`takes_strike_back`, `combat.rs:875`). Base 2/5 with Armor 3 and Pierce: an attacker in its lane takes 10 piercing, one beside it 6. Radiant 4/10 with Armor 6: 28 and 16.
- The forecasts reuse the same call, so they agree with the bug: the combat forecast players see (`crates/engine/src/query.rs:1079`), My Pawn's lethal check (`crates/engine/src/subsystems/lethal.rs:144`) and the AI's attack candidates (`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs:181`).
- No test holds it. `crates/engine/tests/rules/damage_routing.rs:340` (`mod r3554008_sweep`) and Fuse's own tests (`crates/cards/src/scripts/stinkyscape_plus/c107_fuse_unit.rs`) cover only Fuse attacking. No ruling in `spec/rulings/` or §11 decides a defending sweep.
- Stinkyscape+ is in the middle of a run of balance patches (#4154 is open), and Fuse's measured strength includes this bug.

## Proposal

1. In `combat.rs`, separate the weight on a strike back from the weight on an attack. For example, a `strike_back_multiplier_for(state, defender, attacker)` that is `lane_multiplier_for` without its `sweep_weight` step, so Bunker's lane strike stays. Use it at the four strike-back sites: `combat.rs:921`, `query.rs:1079`, `lethal.rs:144` and `candidates.rs:181`. The attacker's hit and `sweep()` stay as they are.
2. Spec: add one sentence to §4.3's Sweep paragraph and to R3554008's note: a Fuse that is attacked strikes back with its plain attack, because the sweep's weight belongs to its attacks alone. Edit R3554008's §11 paragraph where it stands (`spec/11-rulings.md:1908`). The spec already says "its attack", so this clarifies R3554008 under no new number. If the builder reads the spec as silent, it takes the first ruling of the issue's block instead, with the paragraph in `spec/pending/<issue>.md`.
3. Claim the play change with `cargo jackioh patches "<title>" --plays stinkyscapeplus-107` (a micro), as `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` will require. Suggested player note: "Fuse hits back for its printed attack when it is attacked; only its own attacks are multiplied."

## Where it lands

- Code: `crates/engine/src/combat.rs`, `crates/engine/src/query.rs`, `crates/engine/src/subsystems/lethal.rs`, and one line of `crates/ai/src/candidates.rs`.
- Tests: `crates/engine/tests/rules/damage_routing.rs`, `crates/engine/tests/rules/combat_forecast.rs`, `crates/cards/src/scripts/stinkyscape_plus/c107_fuse_unit.rs`, and the AI's candidate test in `crates/ai`.
- Spec: §4.3 (`spec/04-combat.md`), `spec/rulings/R3554008.md`, and R3554008's paragraph in `spec/11-rulings.md`.
- A pending fragment under `crates/cards/patches/pending/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A new `fn r3554008_…` in `damage_routing.rs`: an enemy vanilla Unit in Fuse's lane attacks Fuse and ends with damage equal to Fuse's attack, not five times it. One in an adjacent lane likewise ends with the plain attack, not three times it. No other enemy Unit takes damage.
- [ ] `r3554008_sweep_hits_lane_times_five_adjacent_times_three` passes unchanged.
- [ ] Bunker's lane-strike tests (`c097_5_bunker.rs`, `r1283_struck_back_across_its_lane_it_hits_first_for_15` among them) pass unchanged.
- [ ] The combat forecast for an attack on Fuse shows the plain strike back (`combat_forecast.rs`), and so does the AI's attack candidate on Fuse.
- [ ] Fuse's own tests, when it is attacked: the base face hits back for 2, the Radiant face for 4.
- [ ] Every new test fails on today's code.
- [ ] These pass: `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test 'rules*'`, `cargo test -p jackioh-cards c107_fuse`, `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, `cargo jackioh spec check`, `cargo jackioh patches check` and `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims`.

## Size and risks

Small: a few lines of engine code plus tests, about ten files. It is a combat rule, so the planner may rate it hard.

- Fuse gets weaker in play, and opponents and the AI will attack it more. That is what its text says, but its win rate will move. The owner may want this to land before or with #4154's Stinkyscape+ balance pass.
- Old replays in which someone attacked a Fuse will no longer reach their final hash. R767000 retires games that an engine rule change alters, as it does for any rule fix.
- If the owner wants a defending Fuse to sweep its whole lane rather than only its attacker, that is a different change: a new ruling and a sweep on the strike back. This proposal takes the reading that the card's text and §4.3 give.

| `crates/engine/tests/rules/combat_forecast.rs` | change | One new test proving forecast `taken` |

| `spec/rulings/R3554008.md` | change | Note body gains the same sentence |

## Steps

1. Re-read `spec/04-combat.md` §4.3, `spec/06-keywords.md` §6.3 Sweep row, `spec/rulings/R3554008.md`, and `crates/cards/src/scripts/meditative/c097_5_bunker.rs` (R1283: lane strike multiplies attacking and defending — the behavior to preserve).
2. In `crates/engine/src/combat.rs`, after `lane_multiplier_for` (~line 728), add `pub fn strike_back_multiplier_for(state: &GameState, defender: &CardInstance, attacker: &CardInstance) -> i32` holding the lane-strike body only (the `lane_multiplier` flag read, slot reads, `in_units_row_or_standing` + opposite-sides + `giga::lanes_meet` check, `params::declared_or(state, defender, "multiplier", printed)`), with no `sweep_weight` step. Rewrite `lane_multiplier_for` to keep its sweep early-return, then `return strike_back_multiplier_for(state, striker, struck)`. Update that function's doc comment to say the sweep reads first so `lethal.rs` and `query.rs` agree with combat.
3. Change the four strike-back sites to `strike_back_multiplier_for`, leaving every attacker-side `lane_multiplier_for` call alone: `combat.rs:921` (`resolve_combat`), `query.rs:1079` (`back`), `lethal.rs:144` (`theirs_attack` in `falls_to_first_strike`, which `query.rs` reuses), `candidates.rs:181` (`strike_back` in `exchange`; add the import between `slot_of` and `subsystems`). Do not touch `sweep()` — it already runs only from `strike()`.
4. In `crates/engine/tests/rules/fixtures/combat.rs`, add a `sweeper` fixture after the keyword bodies: id `cb-sweeper`, next free `cb-` index in that file, 2/20 Ranged (mirrors Fuse), plus a scripts entry with `StaticFlags { sweep_lane: Some(5), sweep_adjacent: Some(3) }`, registered in `COMBAT_DEFS` and `COMBAT_SCRIPTS`, following the `spikey_pillow_scripts` pattern.
5. In `crates/engine/tests/rules/damage_routing.rs`, `mod r3554008_sweep`, add `r3554008_attacked_in_its_lane_it_strikes_back_with_its_plain_attack` (p1 FUSE lane 3; p2 PLAIN lane 3 plus BULWARKs lanes 2, 4; `s.end_turn()`; p2 PLAIN attacks FUSE; PLAIN damage is 2 not 10; both BULWARKs 0) and `r3554008_attacked_from_beside_its_lane_it_strikes_back_with_its_plain_attack` (same but PLAIN in lane 2; damage 2 not 6; neighbors 0). Copy the existing test's `board`/`id_at`/`s.attack` usage.
6. In `crates/engine/tests/rules/combat_forecast.rs`, add `mod r3554008_a_defending_sweeper_strikes_back_plain` with `r3554008_the_forecast_strikes_back_a_sweeper_with_its_plain_attack`: `put` plain (3/3) vs sweeper in lane 1, assert `(forecast.dealt, forecast.taken) == (3, 2)`, `survives`, and `PlayedAttack::forecast(&forecast) == play_out(...)`, copying `r3100000_armor_takes_its_part_of_the_blow_and_the_strike_back`.
7. In `c107_fuse_unit.rs`, add `r3554008_attacked_it_strikes_back_with_its_plain_attack` (base) and `r3554008_attacked_the_radiant_strikes_back_with_its_plain_attack` (radiant): p2 field `[TOUGH, TOUGH, "stand-in (1) 6/60", TOUGH, TOUGH]` so the 6-attack stand-in faces Fuse in lane 3; `s.end_turn()`; attack Fuse; assert `lanes(&s) == [0, 0, 2, 0, 0]` base / `[0, 0, 4, 0, 0]` radiant. A non-Ranged attacker is fine: Fuse is Ranged, so `takes_strike_back` answers true.
8. In `crates/ai/src/candidates.rs` `mod tests`, add `r3554008_a_defending_fuse_strikes_back_with_its_plain_attack`: `const FUSE: &str = "stinkyscapeplus-107"`; explicit-lane scenario copying `the_strike_across_a_bunkers_lane_is_multiplied` (VANILLA lane 1 vs FUSE lane 1); assert `(combat.hit, combat.strike_back) == (4, 2)`.
9. Spec: append "A Fuse that is attacked strikes back with its plain attack: the sweep's weight belongs to its attacks alone." to the §4.3 Sweep paragraph (`spec/04-combat.md:46`) and to `spec/rulings/R3554008.md` (front matter unchanged). Write `spec/pending/4156.md` holding the full amended paragraph: `**[[R3554008]] a sweep hits its lane several times over and the adjacent lanes fewer (issue #3554, 2026-11-11)**: 5 times its attack in its lane (Radiant 7), 3 times adjacent (Radiant 4), one instance each; a declared target outside the sweep takes a normal hit. A Fuse that is attacked strikes back with its plain attack: the sweep's weight belongs to its attacks alone.` Do not edit `spec/11-rulings.md` where it stands: CLAUDE.md rule 3 overrules the issue text there, and the fold appends the pending file on `main`.
10. Run `cargo jackioh patches "Fuse strikes back with its printed attack" --plays stinkyscapeplus-107`, hand-write the player note into the new fragment ("Fuse hits back for its printed attack when it is attacked; only its own attacks are multiplied."), keeping every line within the length limit (`patches.rs`, R724001).

## Tests

- `crates/engine/tests/rules/damage_routing.rs`: the two new `r3554008_attacked_…` tests — same-lane attacker ends at 2 damage (was 10), adjacent-lane attacker at 2 (was 6), neighbors at 0.
- `crates/engine/tests/rules/combat_forecast.rs`: new test — forecast `taken` is 2 and matches the played-out attack.
- `crates/cards/src/scripts/stinkyscape_plus/c107_fuse_unit.rs`: new tests — base Fuse struck back for 2, Radiant for 4, no other lane damaged.
- `crates/ai/src/candidates.rs`: new `r3554008_…` test — `exchange` on Fuse gives `strike_back` 2.
- Unchanged behavior: `r3554008_sweep_hits_lane_times_five_adjacent_times_three`, Bunker's `c097_5_bunker` tests (`r1283_struck_back_across_its_lane_it_hits_first_for_15` et al).
- Commands: `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test 'rules*' r3554008`, `cargo test -p jackioh-cards c107_fuse`, `cargo test -p jackioh-cards c097_5_bunker`, `cargo test -p jackioh-ai r3554008`, `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai combat_mods`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-engine -p jackioh-cards -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo jackioh spec check`, `cargo jackioh patches check`, `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims`.

## Done when

- [ ] New `r3554008_…` tests exist in `damage_routing.rs` (same-lane and adjacent), `combat_forecast.rs`, `c107_fuse_unit.rs` (base + Radiant) and `candidates.rs`, and each fails on today's code.
- [ ] The sweep-on-attack test and all Bunker lane-strike tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] Forecast, lethal projection and AI candidates show the plain strike back.
- [ ] `spec check`, `patches check` and `classify --base origin/main --claims` pass.
- [ ] The micro fragment claims `stinkyscapeplus-107` with the player note.

## Risks

- Fuse gets weaker; opponents and the AI will attack it more. Intended per its text, but its win rate moves — may interact with #4154's Stinkyscape+ balance pass.
- Old replays where someone attacked a Fuse no longer reach their final hash; R767000 retires them as for any rule fix.
- The fold appends `spec/pending/4156.md` blindly, so `main` briefly holds two R3554008 §11 paragraphs until the stale line at the old position is removed; the note and §4.3 are the source of truth meanwhile.
- First Strike interplay flows through the same four edited values (defender-first branches in `resolve_combat`, `falls_to_first_strike`), so no separate First Strike change is needed.

## Open questions

- Timing vs #4154's balance pass: land this before or with it, since Fuse's measured strength includes the bug. (Person's call; planned to land standalone.)
- Decisions taken: `lane_multiplier_for` delegates to the new function instead of duplicating the lane-meet body; `spec/pending/4156.md` replaces the issue's direct `spec/11-rulings.md` edit per CLAUDE.md rule 3; a new `sweeper` engine fixture instead of reusing `board_geometry` fixtures or the real Fuse card (wrong catalog for forecast tests); two engine tests rather than one, per the acceptance criteria.
```
